title: C2434 — Steering column lock module
introduction:
This reference maps the steering column lock module’s connector. The module secures the column as part of the theft-deterrent system, where fitted. Its electrical connections have different jobs: the lock needs power, a return path and communication. Think of the communication link as the conversation that tells the lock what to do; electricity alone is not the whole story.

I start with the connector identity, compare the drawing’s housing features, then follow each cavity label into the circuit table. The service-parts tables provide a separate identification reference. This page teaches that reading process, not access, probing, diagnosis or replacement. Physical viewing direction, the gauge convention and the meanings of the Size and Used codes are unspecified, so those fields cannot supply missing test or wire-selection instructions.

edits.why: I use the housing outline and the large rectangular feature at the left to keep my place in this drawing. The cavity circles form a vertical column, with the upper circle shaded. Their labels connect the illustration to the Cavity column below; shading alone is not an electrical test result. The adjacent identity table ties this view to its harness and shell.

Read across a cavity’s row to connect its location with the circuit identifier, color label, gauge, function and terminal part number. The functions distinguish the lock’s positive connection, structural ground and communication link. That link carries messages rather than serving as a simple on/off power wire. The shaded position has blank circuit and function fields; leave those blanks intact rather than assigning it a job.

The pigtail table connects a kit entry with its service part, engineering shell and listed construction details. I compare the engineering-shell entry with the connector identity before carrying a part reference forward. Pigtail gauge and circuit gauge belong to separate entries; this listing does not authorize substituting wire or teach a splice or connector replacement.
